Hatch (1999). Minerals and Metals: Preliminary Analysis of Actions and Opportunities for GHG Mitigation. Final Report, issued 18 June 1999, prepared for the Minerals and Metals Working Group, Industry Issues Table, National Climate Change Process. Hatch, 2800 Speakman Drive, Mississauga, Ontario. Report number not printed on the cover; a separate Summary Report exists.

Region: Canada. Locators are PRINTED page numbers of the form section-page (e.g. p.6-12, "Page" footer). Mostly a measures study: each sub-sector action has a sector-wide capital, NPV, GHG reduction and cost per t GHG at 10% real discount rate in constant 1997 dollars. Those 25 results are in _measures (no per-plant or per-tonne capex, except where stated). Loaded to the main file: aluminium emission factors by smelter technology (Table 6-5), CWPB replacement capex per t (6,000 CA$/t), reheat furnace SEC (older 2,650 and very efficient 1,484 MJ/t), cement upgrade capex per t (242 from wet, 42 from long dry), a new 350 t/day lime kiln (capacity, 6.0 GJ/t, capex 15-25 million), an oxygen smelting furnace (330 million for two, derived 165 each). Not loaded: GHG forecasts, competitiveness tables, indirect actions (lightweight vehicles, concrete housing), appendices of facilities. TRAPS: (1) Several tables and the text disagree: cement process upgrade GHG 9.7 Mt (table) vs 8.8 Mt (text) and NPV +132.5 (table) vs -133 (text); BOF capital 25-100 (table) vs 50-100 (text); aluminium electricity price printed 0.04 cents/kWh (clearly 4 cents); point feeder NPV printed -16 and +16.3. (2) Table 6-5 implies 1990-vintage CF4 rates (0.55, 1.1, 1.0, 0.5 kg/t and 0.25 kg/t for CWPB-300), at odds with nccp_1999_001 and _003. (3) Sect. 10 refers to Table 8-4 and 8-7 for mining actions (copy-paste). (4) The aluminium association comments inline that it rejects the discounting method and the Hatch cost basis. (5) Cement capex per tonne unit basis (annual capacity?) not stated. (6) New lime kiln type is not stated and costs are in 1999 dollars while the rest are constant 1997 dollars.
